agent.result_text:
A hold no longer takes anything out of the totals. Held people's claims and held claims now count everywhere again, and the only thing a hold still does is the pool cut. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**Server**
- `Person.java`: `counts` and `countsAsOf` no longer leave out held claims or claims dated in one of the person's holds. These two rules feed the due-totals, overdue, period figures, backing and rollup lines. `countsClaimed` now just uses `counts`. Retired people and deferred claims are still left out as before.
- `StatementService.java`: a statement no longer leaves out held claims either.
- I updated the comments in `Claim.java` and `RollupService.java` to match.

**Front end**
- `people.ts`: the screen's copy of the counting rules now only checks retirement, which matches the server. I removed the `heldOn` helper because nothing uses it any more.
- `pools.ts` is unchanged. A person on hold on the sheet's today still gets no cut, and their share is spread over the other members.

Holding and releasing a claim, its `CLAIM_HELD` / `CLAIM_RELEASED` audit records, the "on hold" column and adding a person hold all work as before. They just no longer change any figures.

probe.probe_text:
I haven't changed anything. Below, `Java` means `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/` and `FE` means `src/main/frontend/src/app/`.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Per claim (claim row, `FE features/claims/claims.ts`)

| Shown (`data-testid`) | Rule |
|---|---|
| `claim-number` | Given when the claim is opened (`ClaimService.nextNumber`). While `Sheet.numbersByPeriod()` is on (`periodNumberingFrom` ≤ today) it is `<period>-n`, or `X-n` when the due-by falls in no period. Otherwise it is `FYyyyy-n`, one sequence shared by the whole sheet tree (`SheetService.nextClaimNumber`). A REVIEW claim gets its number only when reviewed. Reassign and split take a new number; a voided claim keeps its own. |
| `claim-amount` | Entered. Once a claim has lines, its amount is the sum of qty × unit (`addLine`) and an edit can't change it (`ClaimAmountFromLinesException`). A negative amount is a **correction** (`isCorrection`). |
| `claim-date` | Left blank, a new claim takes `entryDate`, else the sheet's `today`; an edited one takes `today`. It can't be after the person's `retiredFrom` or inside a past retirement (`Person.requireClaimable`). |
| `claim-due-by` | Fixed when the claim is added: `HolidayService.businessDaysAfter(date, terms)`, skipping weekends and holidays. `terms` come from `termsFor`: the person's own `termsOn(today)`, else the grade's `terms-X`, else the sheet's `terms` (starting value 14). Adding a holiday later works the due-by out again for every claim not SETTLED or VOID that is due on or after that holiday. Redate never moves it. |
| `claim-period` | The period the **due-by** falls in, not the period of the date. |
| `claim-due` | `claimDue`, in order: (1) `settledDue` if set; (2) `statedDue` if `stated` (n/a when that is null); (3) otherwise `figure = amount × rate% → 2dp` (`rateStep`/`dueOf`), then raised to `floorOn(date)` (`floored`), then `lateCharge` added on top. A correction gets neither floor nor late charge. No rate gives `n/a`. |
| ↳ rate | `rateOn(grade on claim date, claim date, rateStamp)`. A rate's to-date ends it. If the sheet has no rate in force it falls back to the parent sheets (up to 3 levels, `PARENT_LEVELS`), then the `source` sheet the clone came from. A **forward-only** rate (from-date ≥ today when saved) is only seen by claims added after it was saved (`rateStamp`/`forwardAfter`, `RateVersion`). |
| ↳ rounding | `Sheet.rounding`: the dated `rounding` setting on the claim date if one is set. Otherwise half-up when `roundingDate` is before `policyDate` (or `today` when no policy date), half-even on or after. `roundingDate` is the claim date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects. |
| ↳ late charge | `Sheet.lateCharge`: only for OPEN/PENDING claims that are not waived and not deferred. For each full 30 days `today` is past `overdueBy`, it adds `late-pct` (as in force on that 30-day mark) of the figure plus the earlier charges, so it compounds; each step is rounded. `overdueBy` = due-by + `grace-<grade>` days. |
| `claim-overdue` | OPEN/PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueBy < today`. |
| `claim-stated` | Bound by the person's last statement (`Claim.isBound` = `stated`). |
| `claim-deferred` / `-until` | A claim counts as deferred (`isDeferredOn`) only when it is OPEN and `today < deferredUntil`. While deferred it is in no total, never overdue, has no late charge, can't be settled or split, and a statement leaves it unbound. The row's flag uses `deferralRunning`, which doesn't check for OPEN, so the flag and the rule can disagree. |
| `claim-waived`, `claim-held`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-review-late`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-batch`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-log-line due=` | **Waived:** a steward sets it on an OPEN/PENDING claim; it removes the late charge. **Held:** see "Holds" below. **Late entry:** the due-by fell in a soft-closed period when the claim was added. **Review late:** `reviewOn + reviewSla < today`. **Reminded:** a second reminder on the same day is refused; after an `escalateAfter` gap, one ESCALATE per claim. **Batch:** `settleBatch` is set by a bulk settle. **Log `due=`:** the shown due at that moment (`ClaimService.log`/`shownDue`). |

### Lifecycle and what gets frozen (`ClaimStatus`, `ClaimService`)

- **Status moves:** DRAFT → OPEN, or REVIEW when the due is above `review-threshold` → OPEN → SETTLED, or PENDING when a clerk settles above `clerkLimitFor(grade)`. VOID is allowed from DRAFT, REVIEW, OPEN or PENDING, and from SETTLED only by a steward within `SETTLED_VOID_DAYS` = 7. DELETED is allowed from DRAFT only, and can be restored only on the same `today` it was deleted.
- **Which statuses count:** `counts()` is OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED. `isOpen()` is OPEN and PENDING.
- **Frozen on settle** (`settle`): `settledDue` = the bound due if the claim is bound, else the live due (floor plus late charge as of settling). A correction freezes its bare figure. If there is no rate the due stays live.
  - `settleAsOf` freezes the due as it stood at the end of a past date.
  - `resettle` (steward only) freezes it again at today's figures, as if open and unbound.
  - `approve` freezes it the same way as `settle`.
- **Statement** (`StatementService.take`): records the person's due-total, capped, and binds every counting claim to its shown due (`setStated(true, due)`). All other claims are unbound. Reassigning or splitting a claim unbinds it. `cancelLast` (steward only) unbinds and does not restore an earlier binding.
- **Who may do what:**
  - **Matrix:** `Sheet.allows`/`STANDING_PERMISSIONS` decide open, settle and void (clerk or steward), reassign (steward), close (clerk or steward) and reopen (steward).
  - **Roles:** a name with no role is a clerk (`RoleService.roleOf`). A delegation that covers today makes the user a steward. A VIEWER is blocked from every change (`ViewerInterceptor`), and an archived sheet blocks every change (`ArchivedInterceptor`).
  - **Steward only:** review, resettle, waive, redate, flag, cancel a statement, lock a period, void a settled claim.
  - **Four eyes:** whoever opened or last edited a claim can't settle or approve it. `settlePart` judges this on the original claim.
  - **Pending claims:** a steward or the person's `approver` approves or rejects them.
  - **Flagged person** (`flagOn(today)`): only a steward may open or split their claims.
- **Gates checked on the due:**
  - `requireProof`: a due above `proof-threshold-<grade>`/`proof-threshold` on the claim date needs a proof, plus one of each `proofKinds`.
  - `requireNote`: a due above `note-threshold` needs a note.
  - `requireUnderCap`: a period's `cap` limits how many OPEN or PENDING claims a person may have in it.
  - A correction must name a SETTLED claim of the same person and can't exceed what remains of it (`requireCorrection`).
- **Closed periods:** `PeriodService.requireOpen(dueBy)` refuses every add, edit, status change, defer, waive, redate, reassign, split, proof and line on a claim whose due-by is in a closed period.
  - **Soft-close** fixes the figures but still allows changes; new claims added then are marked late entries.
  - **Close** fixes `personTotals`, `personCarried` and `closedTotal` (`Period.fix`).
  - `autoClose` runs when `today` moves past `to + graceDays`.
  - **Lock** only blocks reopen.

### Per person (person row, `FE features/people/people.ts`)

- **Live counting** (`live` in the front end, `Person.counts` in Java): OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED, not deferred. An open claim is also left out once `retiredFrom ≤ today`, unless it is bound.
- **`person-claimed`:** the sum of the amounts of live claims, excluding corrections (`claimedBy`).
- **`person-due-total`:** the sum of `claimDue` over live claims, skipping n/a, then held down to `cap` (`capped`).
  - It is `n/a` when the grade in force today has no rate today, unless some counting claim has a fixed due or has a due and is dated on or before today.
  - `excessOf` = how far the total is above the cap.
- **`person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`:** live dues of SETTLED claims / of OPEN+PENDING claims. Neither is capped.
- **`person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`:** the live claims that are overdue, and their dues.
- **Aged buckets 0–30 / 31–60 / 61+:** open live dues, by how many days old the claim's date is.
- **`person-period-<name>-due-total`:**
  - Closed or soft-closed period: the fixed figure, or 0.00 for someone added since.
  - Open period: dues of claims whose due-by is in the period and whose status at the end of the period's last day (from the status log, `statusOn`/`liveAtEnd`) was counting.
- **Carried figure** (`carriedOf`): for an open period, dues of claims from earlier periods that were still open at its end, plus the **opening balance** from `OpeningImportService`. That import only adds to the openings, all lines or none.
- **Statement columns** (`person-stated-total`, statement count and date): from `StatementSummary`.
- **Backing:** each patron's SETTLED dues over the last 90 days × share ÷ 100, rounded half-even.
- **Cut total:** comes from the pools.
- **Grade shown:** `gradeOn(today)`.

### Holds

The comments disagree with each other about what a hold does. `Claim.held` says a held claim "still counts in every total". `toggleHold` says it "leaves the live totals". The front end's `Person.holds` says held OPEN/PENDING claims "count in no live total".

What the code actually does: `Person.counts`/`live` ignore holds, and `heldOn`/`heldAsOf` are never called. A person's hold only removes them from pool cuts (`pools.ts`). A claim's hold only shows the `claim-held` flag and writes an audit line.

### Imports

- **People** (`ImportPeopleService`): a line matching an existing name or alias updates that person, with the grade recorded from today; any other line adds a person. A blank grade takes `defaultGrade`.
- **Claims** (`PasteClaimsService`): adds and opens a claim per line, and reuses a matching DRAFT where it finds one.
- **Rates** (`ImportRatesService`): sets each rate the way the rate form would.
- **Openings:** described under the carried figure above.

All four imports are all-or-nothing.

### Sheet totals

- `rollup-claimed-total` is the plain sum of everyone's claimed.
- `rollup-due-total` and `rollup-overdue-total` use `trimmedSumDues`: with three or more people, the single highest and lowest are dropped.
- Settled and open totals are not trimmed.
- The consolidated total adds the descendant sheets' figures.
- Tag and month totals sum live dues.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

Hard. The rules are scattered and duplicated, not kept in one place. The due calculation alone is written at least four times:
- `Sheet.liveDue`/`ClaimService.liveDue` (used for gates and settling)
- `RollupService.dueOf` (audit ROLLUP/TOTALS lines and period close)
- `StatementService.figureOf`/`take`
- the TypeScript `claimDue`/`lateCharge`/`rateOn` (what the screen actually shows)

The "which claims count" and "n/a" rules are duplicated the same way. Some comments contradict the code (holds especially), and small differences have crept in between copies (e.g. `deferralRunning` vs `isDeferredOn`). A new developer would have to read about five large files across two languages and check them against each other to know what any figure really means.
